speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Law how has the Legal Aid Bureau made provisions to offer non-digital access to its services to applicants who may be illiterate, of low-income or not digitally able.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because often us as Members of Parliament, even after we make an appeal for legal assistance or aid or advice, and specifying that our our residents are not digital savvy, they are not proficient in English, they are elderly, and so forth, we will still get a template reply to "please refer to the portal".

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I thought, if there are already services available such as these, that we can actually communicate a lot better.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And also to the ground, perhaps resource even more the SSOs or the Community Clubs because they are also manned or staffed by public servants and so, the security or privacy considerations are better managed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I ask for therefore better communication and really looking to this challenge on the ground.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And I will certainly bring the feedback back to my colleagues.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
